Terms & Conditions

Tour Cancellation and Refund Policy
At Summit Experts Adventure Tours, we understand that travel plans may change due to unforeseen circumstances. To ensure transparency and fairness, we have outlined our tour cancellation and refund policy below. Please review the terms carefully before booking your adventure.


1. Sightseeing Tours
If you need to cancel your sightseeing tour, we offer a refund of your deposit amount, minus a 10% administrative fee. To request a cancellation, please notify us as soon as possible. You may also transfer your deposit to another products of Summit Experts tours within the next two years without any deduction in your deposit amount.


2. Treks and Expeditions
For treks and expedition bookings, the deposit amount is non-refundable. However, if you need to cancel, you can carry forward your reservation for up to two years from the original booking date.
• Rescheduling Option: You may transfer your deposit to another trek or expedition within the next two years.
• No Refunds: Due to the extensive logistical arrangements involved, we cannot provide refunds on deposit payments for treks and expeditions.
For all cancellations, please contact us as early as possible to explore your options. If you have any questions regarding our refund and cancellation policy, feel free to reach out to our team.


3. Cancellation by Summit Experts Adventure Tours
We reserve the right to cancel a tour due to unforeseen circumstances such as natural disasters, government restrictions, safety concerns, or insufficient group size. In such cases:
• Clients will receive a full refund or may opt for an alternative trip of equal value.
• If the cancellation occurs due to force majeure (e.g., political instability, pandemics, extreme weather), refunds will be processed after deducting non-recoverable costs.


4. Changes and Modifications
• If a client wishes to change their booking to a different date or tour, requests must be made at least 30 days before departure (for sightseeing tours) and 45 days before departure (for adventure treks/expeditions). Additional charges may apply based on the modifications.
• Changes requested within a shorter period (7-days) will be treated as cancellations and subject to the above refund policies if “we” are not able to entertain your modifications and changes.

 
5. No-Show Policy
• If a client fails to arrive on the scheduled departure date without prior notice, no refund will be issued.


6. Refund Processing
• Refunds will be processed within 15 business days of the cancellation request.
• Refunds will be issued via the original payment method unless otherwise agreed.
• Transaction fees, bank charges, and non-recoverable costs will be deducted from the refund amount.


7. Travel Insurance
We strongly recommend that all clients obtain comprehensive travel insurance covering trip cancellations, medical emergencies, and personal liabilities.


By booking a tour with Summit Experts Adventure Tours, clients acknowledge and agree to the terms outlined in this policy.
For any questions or cancellation requests, please contact us at info@thesummitexperts.com

Overview

About Tirich Mir Peak

At 7,708 meters, Tirich Mir is the highest mountain in the Hindu Kush range, located in the beautiful Chitral Valley of Pakistan. First climbed by a Norwegian expedition in 1950, it remains a prized goal for serious mountaineers. The ascent is technically demanding, involving challenging glacier crossings and hidden crevasses, making it ideal for experienced climbers seeking true adventure. Rich in local legends and cultural significance, Tirich Mir promises not just a climb, but a journey into one of Pakistan’s most legendary landscapes.

Why This Tour?

  • Experienced expedition logistics team.
  • Strong local connections for hassle-free operations.
  • High-quality meals and equipment at base camp.
  • Professional support for both independent and guided climbers.
  • Reliable weather forecasting and emergency assistance.
  • Commitment to environmental sustainability and responsible tourism.

FAQs

01

What is Tirich Mir?

+

Tirich Mir is the highest peak in the Hindu Kush mountain range, standing at 7,708 meters (25,289 feet). It is located in Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

02

Where is Tirich Mir located?

+

Tirich Mir is situated in the Arkari Valley of the Chitral District, close to Pakistan’s border with Afghanistan.

03

How difficult is it to climb Tirich Mir?

+

Tirich Mir is considered a technically challenging peak due to its deep crevasses, glacier crossings, and unpredictable weather. It is recommended for experienced climbers with prior high-altitude mountaineering experience.

04

When is the best time to climb Tirich Mir?

+

The best climbing season for Tirich Mir is from late June to early September, when the weather conditions are relatively more stable.

05

How long does the Tirich Mir expedition take?

+

The complete expedition takes around 40 days, including travel, trekking, acclimatization, climbing, and return.

06

What level of fitness and experience is required?

+

Participants should have excellent physical fitness and previous experience with high-altitude climbing, preferably on peaks above 6,000 meters.

07

What is included in the expedition package?

+

Typically, the package includes domestic transfers, accommodation, meals, permits, staff support, porters, climbing guides, and group equipment. (Please confirm exact inclusions with your operator.)

08

What kind of weather should I expect?

+

Weather conditions can vary dramatically, from warm days at lower elevations to extremely cold and windy conditions at higher altitudes. Sudden weather changes are common.

09

Will supplemental oxygen be used?

+

Supplemental oxygen is generally not used for Tirich Mir expeditions. Proper acclimatization and physical preparation are key.

10

What kind of accommodation will be provided?

+

Accommodation includes hotels in Islamabad, Chitral, and Peshawar, while during trekking and at base camp, tented accommodations are provided.

11

What permits are required?

+

Climbers need a permit issued by Pakistan’s Ministry of Tourism. We will arrange all necessary paperwork, including briefing and debriefing sessions.

12

Are there any age restrictions?

+

There is no strict age limit, but climbers must be in excellent health and have the necessary physical conditioning and mountaineering skills.

13

What is the group size for this expedition?

+

Groups are usually kept small, between 6 to 12 climbers, to maintain safety, flexibility, and a personalized experience.

14

How are emergencies handled during the expedition?

+

Our team is equipped with satellite phones and radios. In case of an emergency, evacuation plans will be activated immediately.

15

What is the success rate for summiting Tirich Mir?

+

Tirich Mir is challenging, and success largely depends on the climber’s experience, fitness, and weather conditions.

16

How do you ensure environmental responsibility?

+

We strictly follow Leave No Trace principles, ensuring all waste is properly managed and that we protect the fragile mountain environment.

17

How should I prepare for the expedition?

+

Preparation should focus on cardiovascular endurance, strength training, glacier travel practice, and previous high-altitude climbing experience.

18

Are there any extra costs not included in the package?

+

Personal gear, international flights, insurance, visa fees, personal expenses, tips for staff, and meals outside the program are usually not included.

TOUR EXLCUSION/INCLUSION

01

What You Get?

+

Base Camp Services Only:

This package is for climbers who prefer to handle their own high-altitude logistics but need comprehensive support at base camp.

Includes:

  1. Permit Arrangements: Climbing permit for Tirich Mir Peak, liaison officer, environmental fee.
  2. Accommodation & Meals: Hotels in Islamabad and Chitral (B/B), three meals per day at base camp.
  3. Transportation: Domestic flights (Islamabad-Chitral-Islamabad), and jeep transport.
  4. Base Camp Setup: Spacious tents, dining tent, kitchen tent, toilet tent, solar charging.
  5. Kitchen Services: Professional base camp cook, kitchen staff, gas, utensils.
  6. Logistics & Communication: Porters for group equipment, base camp internet and communication setup.
  7. Support Staff: Liaison officer, assistant staff, permit paperwork, briefing/debriefing.
  8. Weather Updates: Regular weather forecast updates.
  9. Medical Support: Basic first aid kit at base camp.
  10. Garbage Management: Waste disposal as per environmental regulations.
  11. Security Clearance: Coordination with local authorities.
  12. BC Generator: Generator for charging electronic devices.
  13. Mess Tent Facilities: Comfortable dining arrangements.
  14. Personal Tent at BC: Individual sleeping tents.
  15. Dining & Lounge Facilities: Proper seating arrangement.
  16. Porterage: For group and personal luggage to base camp.
  17. Satellite Phone Access: Available on a per-minute charge.
  18. Insurance of Staff: Coverage for base camp staff.
  19. Assistance with Customs Clearance: For expedition cargo.
  20. Photography & Documentation Assistance: Support for media requirements.
  21. Expedition Briefing & Debriefing: Assistance with official processes.

Full Board Services:

This package includes base camp services plus high-altitude logistics for climbers needing full support.

Includes:

  1. Everything in Base Camp Services, plus:
  2. High-Altitude Equipment & Support: Fixed ropes, anchors, climbing permits, route fixing costs.
  3. High-Altitude One to One Guide (HAGs): 1 Pakistani climbing guide per member.
  4. High-Altitude Meals & Gas: Pre-packed meals for higher camps, stoves, gas refills.
  5. Oxygen Support (if required at extra cost): Oxygen cylinders, mask, and regulator rental.
  6. Rescue Assistance: Coordination for emergency evacuation and medical assistance.
  7. Personal Climbing Sherpa (if required at extra cost).
  8. Tent at Higher Camps: Provision of tents for high-altitude camps.
  9. Sleeping Mats & Cooking Equipment: For high camps.
  10. Rope Fixing Charges: Shared costs for rope fixing on the route.
  11. Load Carrying to High Camps: Distribution of essential supplies.
  12. Climbing Permit Coordination: Smooth permit processing.
  13. Medical Kit for High Altitude: Advanced first aid provisions.
  14. Weather Forecasting Services: Specialized weather updates for summit push.
  15. Daily Communication with BC & Team Coordination.
  16. Garbage Collection at High Camps: Waste disposal according to environmental regulations.
  17. Summit Push Planning & Strategy Assistance.
  18. High Camp Fuel & Stoves.
  19. Safety Equipment & Coordination for Team Members.
02

What You Don’t?

+
  • International airfare to/from Pakistan.
  • Personal climbing gear (boots, harness, ice axe, crampons, etc.).
  • Personal insurance (medical, travel, evacuation, etc.).
  • Extra hotel nights in case of delays (bad weather, permit issues, etc.).
  • Additional meals in cities beyond itinerary.
  • Personal expenses (laundry, phone calls, internet, extra snacks, drinks, souvenirs, etc.).
  • Emergency evacuation costs (helicopter rescue, medical treatment, hospitalization, etc.).
  • Summit bonus for high-altitude porters and staff (recommended but not included).
  • Oxygen equipment (can be arranged at additional cost).
  • Personal climbing Sherpa (can be arranged at additional cost).
  • Any costs arising due to natural disasters, political instability, or unexpected itinerary changes.
  • Costs due to delays in flights or road transport.
  • Any other services not mentioned in the inclusions.

Overview

About This Trip

Embark on an extraordinary journey through Pakistan’s most iconic UNESCO World Heritage Sites and tentative sites, spanning ancient civilizations, Mughal masterpieces, and cultural landmarks. This 12-day adventure takes you from the bustling capital of Islamabad to the vibrant city of Karachi, covering the awe-inspiring archaeological remains of Mohenjo-Daro, the majestic Lahore Fort, the grand Rohtas Fort, and the mystical Makli Necropolis. Explore the rich legacy of the Gandhara civilization in Taxila, marvel at the architectural brilliance of Shalimar Gardens, and witness the historical grandeur of Derawar Fort in the Cholistan Desert. Each destination offers a unique glimpse into Pakistan’s diverse cultural and historical tapestry, making this tour a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

Why This Tour?

  • UNESCO World Heritage Focus: Immerse yourself in the grandeur of 6 UNESCO-listed sites and several tentative UNESCO sites, offering a comprehensive exploration of Pakistan’s cultural heritage.
  • Expert-Guided Insights: Gain in-depth knowledge with the help of experienced guides who bring the stories behind these historical wonders to life.
  • Cultural Diversity: Discover Pakistan’s rich cultural mosaic through ancient ruins, Mughal architecture, and spiritual landmarks, spanning thousands of years of history.
  • Seamless Travel Experience: Enjoy a well-planned itinerary with comfortable accommodations, domestic flights, and private transfers for a stress-free and immersive experience.
  • Iconic Destinations: From the ancient Indus Valley Civilization at Mohenjo-Daro to the majestic Lahore Fort, experience the architectural marvels and historic treasures that define Pakistan’s identity.
  • Local Experiences: Explore vibrant bazaars, savor traditional Pakistani cuisine, and interact with local artisans to deepen your cultural immersion.

Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad

  • Arrival at Islamabad International Airport
  • Meet and greet, transfer to hotel
  • Visit Pakistan Monument and Lok Virsa Museum
  • Explore Saidpur Village for cultural experience
  • Dinner at Monal Restaurant with a panoramic view of Islamabad
  • Overnight stay in Islamabad

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 2: Taxila – The Ancient Buddhist Civilization (UNESCO Site)

  • Breakfast at hotel
  • Drive to Taxila, a major center of Gandhara civilization
  • Visit Taxila Museum, Dharmarajika Stupa, Sirkap, and Jaulian Monastery
  • Return to Islamabad
  • Visit Shah Faisal Mosque and Daman-e-Koh viewpoint
  • Overnight stay in Islamabad

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Islamabad Serena Hotel
  • Luxury: Roomy Signature Hotel
  • Standard: Grand Islamabad Hotel

Day 3: Rohtas Fort – The Mighty Fortress (UNESCO Site)

  • Drive to Rohtas Fort, a 16th-century fortress built by Sher Shah Suri
  • Explore its Haveli Man Singh, Sohail Gate, and Talaqi Gate
  • Return to Islamabad
  • Flight to Lahore in the evening
  • Overnight stay in Lahore

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Nishat Hotel Gulberg, Lahore
  • Luxury: Luxus Grand Hotel
  • Standard: Lahore Grand Hotel

Day 4: Lahore – The Mughal Marvel (UNESCO Site)

  • Breakfast at hotel
  • Visit Lahore Fort and Shalimar Gardens (both UNESCO sites)
  • Explore Badshahi Mosque and Minar-e-Pakistan
  • Visit Wazir Khan Mosque and Delhi Gate Bazaar
  • Enjoy traditional dinner at Cuckoo’s Den or Haveli Restaurant
  • Overnight stay in Lahore

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Nishat Hotel Gulberg, Lahore
  • Luxury: Luxus Grand Hotel
  • Standard: Lahore Grand Hotel

Day 5: Harappa – The Indus Valley Civilization

  • Drive to Harappa, one of the ancient sites of the Indus Valley Civilization
  • Explore the Harappa Museum and ruins
  • Drive to Multan in the evening
  • Visit Multan’s shrines if time permits
  • Overnight stay in Multan

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Ramada By Wyndham/Rumanzan by PC Hotel
  • Luxury: Hotel One Multan
  • Standard: Hotel Avalon Suites, Multan

Day 6: Multan – The City of Saints

  • Breakfast at hotel
  • Visit Shah Rukn-e-Alam’s Tomb and Bahauddin Zakariya Shrine
  • Explore Multan Fort and Ghanta Ghar
  • Drive to Bahawalpur in the afternoon
  • Visit Noor Mahal
  • Overnight stay in Bahawalpur

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 7: Uch Sharif & Derawar Fort

  • Drive to Uch Sharif, home to the Shrine of Bibi Jawindi (Tentative UNESCO Site)
  • Continue to Derawar Fort, a grand 9th-century fortress in the Cholistan Desert
  • Return to Bahawalpur
  • Overnight stay in Bahawalpur

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 8: Drive to Sukkur & Mohenjo-Daro – The Cradle of Civilization (UNESCO Site)

  • Early morning drive from Bahawalpur to Sukkur
  • Visit Mohenjo-Daro, one of the main sites of the Indus Valley Civilization
  • Explore the Stupa, Great Bath, and Granary
  • Overnight stay in Sukkur

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hotel One Sukkur/RT Grace Royal Taj Hotel
  • Luxury: Hotel Hayatt, Sukkur
  • Standard: Pakistan Club Inn Hotel

Day 9: Makli Necropolis & Shah Jahan Mosque (UNESCO Site)

  • Drive to Thatta
  • Visit Makli Necropolis, one of the largest cemeteries in the world
  • Explore Shah Jahan Mosque, known for its exquisite tile work
  • Drive to Karachi
  • Overnight stay in Karachi

Stay Options:

  • Premium: PC Hotel, Karachi/Avari Tower
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 10: Karachi & Chaukhandi Tombs (Tentative UNESCO Site)

  • Visit Quaid-e-Azam’s Mausoleum and Mohatta Palace
  • Explore Chaukhandi Tombs, known for their intricate sandstone carvings
  • Visit Clifton Beach and Port Grand
  • Overnight stay in Karachi

Stay Options:

  • Premium: PC Hotel, Karachi/Avari Tower
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 11: Hingol National Park & Princess of Hope (Tentative UNESCO Site)

  • Full-day excursion to Hingol National Park in Balochistan
  • Visit Princess of Hope rock formation and Hinglaj Mata Temple
  • Enjoy scenic views of the Makran Coastal Highway
  • Return to Karachi
  • Overnight stay in Karachi

Stay Options:

  • Premium: PC Hotel, Karachi/Avari Tower
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 12: Departure from Karachi

  • Breakfast at hotel
  • Free time for shopping at Dolmen Mall or Zainab Market
  • Transfer to Karachi International Airport for departure

  • Drive to Rohtas Fort, a 16th-century fortress built by Sher Shah Suri
  • Explore its Haveli Man Singh, Sohail Gate, and Talaqi Gate
  • Return to Islamabad
  • Flight to Lahore in the evening
  • Overnight stay in Lahore

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Nishat Hotel Gulberg, Lahore
  • Luxury: Luxus Grand Hotel
  • Standard: Lahore Grand Hotel

Day 4: Lahore – The Mughal Marvel (UNESCO Site)

  • Breakfast at hotel
  • Visit Lahore Fort and Shalimar Gardens (both UNESCO sites)
  • Explore Badshahi Mosque and Minar-e-Pakistan
  • Visit Wazir Khan Mosque and Delhi Gate Bazaar
  • Enjoy traditional dinner at Cuckoo’s Den or Haveli Restaurant
  • Overnight stay in Lahore

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Nishat Hotel Gulberg, Lahore
  • Luxury: Luxus Grand Hotel
  • Standard: Lahore Grand Hotel

Day 5: Harappa – The Indus Valley Civilization

  • Drive to Harappa, one of the ancient sites of the Indus Valley Civilization
  • Explore the Harappa Museum and ruins
  • Drive to Multan in the evening
  • Visit Multan’s shrines if time permits
  • Overnight stay in Multan

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Ramada By Wyndham/Rumanzan by PC Hotel
  • Luxury: Hotel One Multan
  • Standard: Hotel Avalon Suites, Multan

Day 6: Multan – The City of Saints

  • Breakfast at hotel
  • Visit Shah Rukn-e-Alam’s Tomb and Bahauddin Zakariya Shrine
  • Explore Multan Fort and Ghanta Ghar
  • Drive to Bahawalpur in the afternoon
  • Visit Noor Mahal
  • Overnight stay in Bahawalpur

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 7: Uch Sharif & Derawar Fort

  • Drive to Uch Sharif, home to the Shrine of Bibi Jawindi (Tentative UNESCO Site)
  • Continue to Derawar Fort, a grand 9th-century fortress in the Cholistan Desert
  • Return to Bahawalpur
  • Overnight stay in Bahawalpur

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 8: Drive to Sukkur & Mohenjo-Daro – The Cradle of Civilization (UNESCO Site)

  • Early morning drive from Bahawalpur to Sukkur
  • Visit Mohenjo-Daro, one of the main sites of the Indus Valley Civilization
  • Explore the Stupa, Great Bath, and Granary
  • Overnight stay in Sukkur

Stay Options:

  • Premium: Hotel One Sukkur/RT Grace Royal Taj Hotel
  • Luxury: Hotel Hayatt, Sukkur
  • Standard: Pakistan Club Inn Hotel

Day 9: Makli Necropolis & Shah Jahan Mosque (UNESCO Site)

  • Drive to Thatta
  • Visit Makli Necropolis, one of the largest cemeteries in the world
  • Explore Shah Jahan Mosque, known for its exquisite tile work
  • Drive to Karachi
  • Overnight stay in Karachi

Stay Options:

  • Premium: PC Hotel, Karachi/Avari Tower
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 10: Karachi & Chaukhandi Tombs (Tentative UNESCO Site)

  • Visit Quaid-e-Azam’s Mausoleum and Mohatta Palace
  • Explore Chaukhandi Tombs, known for their intricate sandstone carvings
  • Visit Clifton Beach and Port Grand
  • Overnight stay in Karachi

Stay Options:

  • Premium: PC Hotel, Karachi/Avari Tower
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 11: Hingol National Park & Princess of Hope (Tentative UNESCO Site)

  • Full-day excursion to Hingol National Park in Balochistan
  • Visit Princess of Hope rock formation and Hinglaj Mata Temple
  • Enjoy scenic views of the Makran Coastal Highway
  • Return to Karachi
  • Overnight stay in Karachi

Stay Options:

  • Premium: PC Hotel, Karachi/Avari Tower
  • Luxury: Hotel One Bahawalpur
  • Standard: Hotel Executive Lodges

Day 12: Departure from Karachi

  • Breakfast at hotel
  • Free time for shopping at Dolmen Mall or Zainab Market
  • Transfer to Karachi International Airport for departure

Packing List

📅 General Essentials (For All Months)
  • Travel Documents: Passport, visa, copies (digital and physical)
  • Currency: Pakistani Rupee (PKR) and internationally accepted debit/credit cards
  • Electronics: Mobile phone, charger, power bank, universal adapter, and camera
  • Personal Items: Toiletries, prescription medications, sunglasses, sunscreen (SPF 50+), insect repellent
  • Reusable Water Bottle: For hydration during long journeys
  • Daypack: For daily essentials during excursions
  • Notebook/Pen: For taking notes and recording experiences
☀️ Spring & Early Summer (March – Mid-April)
  • Clothing:
    • Light layers (cotton shirts, long-sleeved tops)
    • Light jacket or fleece (for cool mornings and evenings)
    • Comfortable pants/jeans or long skirts (for cultural sensitivity)
    • Scarf/shawl (for religious sites and modesty)
    • Closed-toe shoes (for uneven terrain at archaeological sites)
  • Optional:
    • Lightweight rain jacket (occasional spring showers)
    • Sunglasses and a light hat for sun protection
☀️ Peak Summer (Mid-April – October)
  • Clothing:
    • Lightweight, breathable fabrics (cotton/linen shirts, loose trousers, dresses)
    • Short sleeves (except when visiting religious sites—carry a light scarf for coverage)
    • Comfortable sandals or open-toe shoes (for walking in the heat)
    • Sun hat or cap (for strong sun protection)
  • Optional:
    • Cooling towel (for hot areas like Mohenjo-Daro and Cholistan Desert)
    • Sunscreen (SPF 50+) and insect repellent (for outdoor excursions)
    • Swimwear (for hotel pools in major cities)

Note: Temperatures can reach 40°C (104°F) in southern Pakistan (e.g., Mohenjo-Daro, Bahawalpur). Pack accordingly for extreme heat.

🍁 Autumn (October – November)
  • Clothing:
    • Light layers (cotton shirts during the day)
    • Light jacket or cardigan (for chilly evenings)
    • Comfortable closed-toe shoes (for archaeological and city sites)
    • Scarf/shawl (for religious and cultural sites)
  • Optional:
    • Moisturizer and lip balm (for drier air in northern regions)
    • Light gloves (for cooler evenings in late November)
❄️ Winter (December – February)
  • Clothing:
    • Warm layers (thermal base layers, sweaters, or fleece jackets)
    • Insulated windproof jacket (for cold mornings and nights)
    • Woolen scarf, gloves, and beanie (especially for Rohtas Fort and northern areas)
    • Thick socks and closed-toe shoes or insulated boots (for comfort and warmth)
  • Optional:
    • Hand warmers (for colder regions)
    • Moisturizer and lip balm (to prevent dry skin)

Note: Temperatures in northern and central Pakistan can drop to 5°C (41°F) or lower during winter nights. Southern Pakistan remains milder.

📸 Special Equipment (Optional, Year-Round)
  • Binoculars: For birdwatching in Hingol National Park
  • Camera Gear: Extra batteries, memory cards, lens cleaning kit
  • Guidebooks/Maps: For deeper exploration of UNESCO sites

Key Information

  • UNESCO Sites Visited: 7 (including Taxila, Lahore Fort & Shalimar Gardens, Rohtas Fort, Mohenjo-Daro, Makli Necropolis, Shah Jahan Mosque, and Hingol National Park).
  • Tentative UNESCO Sites: 3 (Uch Sharif, Chaukhandi Tombs, and Hinglaj Mata Temple).
  • Tour Duration: 12 Days / 11 Nights.
  • Highest Altitude: ~ 710 m (Islamabad Region).
  • Best Seasons:
    • Spring: March – April (Pleasant weather, blooming landscapes).
    • Autumn: October – November (Mild temperatures, ideal for exploration).
    • Winter: December – February (Cool and crisp, best for southern Pakistan).
    • Summer: May – September (Warm to hot, suitable for northern and central regions).
  • Difficulty Level: Moderate – Includes long drives and moderate walking at archaeological sites. Suitable for history enthusiasts and cultural travelers.
  • Entry Requirements:
    • Valid passport with a visa (for international travelers).
    • Domestic travelers require a valid CNIC (National Identity Card).
  • Connectivity: Internet and mobile coverage available in major cities; limited in remote areas like Hingol National Park.
  • Languages Spoken: Urdu (widely spoken), English (in major cities and tourist areas), local dialects in rural regions.
  • Climate Variation:
    • Northern Pakistan (Islamabad, Taxila, Rohtas): Cool winters, warm summers.
    • Southern Pakistan (Mohenjo-Daro, Karachi): Mild winters, hot summers.

FAQs

01

What is included in the tour package?

+

The package typically includes:

  • Accommodation (based on your selected category).
  • All airport transfers and ground transportation.
  • Guided tours at UNESCO and cultural sites.
  • Entrance fees to all listed attractions.
  • Daily breakfast (with other meals depending on package).
  • Domestic flight from Islamabad to Lahore.
02

What is not included in the tour package?

+
  • International airfare to and from Pakistan.
  • Visa fees and processing.
  • Personal expenses (souvenirs, snacks, laundry).
  • Travel insurance (highly recommended).
  • Optional excursions or activities outside the itinerary.
03

What kind of accommodation is provided?

+

We offer three categories:

  • Premium: Luxury hotels such as Serena or Pearl Continental.
  • Luxury: Boutique and 4-star accommodations.
  • Standard: Clean and comfortable mid-range hotels.
04

Is this tour suitable for all age groups?

+

Yes, the tour is suitable for most age groups. However, it involves moderate walking and some long drives, which may be challenging for very young children or those with mobility concerns.

05

Do I need a visa to travel to Pakistan?

+

Yes, most travelers require a visa to enter Pakistan. We can assist you with the application process and provide supporting documentation upon booking.

06

What is the best time to take this tour?

+
  • Spring (March–April): Pleasant weather and blooming landscapes.
  • Autumn (October–November): Mild temperatures, ideal for exploring.
  • Winter (December–February): Best for southern sites like Mohenjo-Daro and Karachi.
  • Summer (May–September): Warm but manageable, ideal for northern areas.
07

Is the tour customizable?

+

Yes, we can tailor the tour to match your preferences, including extending your stay, adjusting activities, or upgrading accommodation.

08

What should I pack for the tour?

+
  • Spring/Autumn: Light layers, a jacket, sunscreen, and comfortable walking shoes.
  • Summer: Light, breathable clothing, a hat, sunglasses, and sunblock.
  • Winter: Warm layers, a heavy coat (especially for the north), and gloves.
09

How safe is it to travel to these areas?

+

The itinerary covers secure and tourist-friendly regions. We prioritize your safety and monitor local conditions continuously. Local guides ensure a smooth and safe experience.

10

Will there be English-speaking guides?

+

Yes, all our guides are fluent in English and knowledgeable about Pakistan’s UNESCO heritage and cultural history.

11

Are there any physical activity requirements?

+

Moderate walking is involved, especially at archaeological sites. Some sites like Rohtas Fort and Mohenjo-Daro require walking on uneven terrain.

12

What is the group size for this tour?

+

Group sizes typically range from 6 to 15 people for a comfortable and personalized experience. Private tours can also be arranged.

13

What kind of food will be provided?

+

The tour includes a mix of local Pakistani cuisine and international options. We accommodate dietary restrictions with advance notice.

14

Is photography allowed at UNESCO sites?

+

Yes, photography is generally allowed. However, some areas (like museums) may restrict flash or drone usage.

15

How can I book this tour?

+

You can book via our website or contact our customer service team. A deposit is required to confirm your booking.

TOUR EXLCUSION/INCLUSION

01

What You Get?

+
  • Road transport 
  • Hotel accommodation according to the itinerary
  • Meals (Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner)
  • Professional Guide
  • Site Tickets
  • Invitation Letter and Other Visa Processing Documents
  • Experienced Driver
  • Driver's food & Accommodation
  • Parking Fees & Toll Taxes
02

What You Don’t?

+
  • Anything not included in the above list
  • International airfare for overseas Pakistani
  • Personal equipment (warm clothes, boots, etc)
  • Tips for guides, porters, staff, etc
  • Miscellaneous (drinks, phone calls, laundry, souvenirs, etc)

 Olena B 
 
 
 
 Verified 
A Journey to Remember
I just returned from an incredible month-long adventure in northern Pakistan with Summit Experts Adventure Tours. We trekked through some of the most breathtaking regions: Skardu, Hunza, Shimshal Village, and made our way to Shimshal Pass, ending with the exhilarating summit of Manglik Sar (6050m). From the very first moment, I knew I was in the hands of true professionals. The entire trip was perfectly organized, from the logistics to safety measures. But what truly made this experience stand out was the team. Every single person was warm, supportive, and treated me like family. Over the course of the trek, they all became a second family to me, and I genuinely feel like I’ve made lifelong friends. The beauty of the Karakoram combined with the knowledge, passion, and dedication of the Summit Experts team made this adventure unforgettable. I felt supported, safe, and inspired every single day. I don’t add pictures, because you MUST visit and see all the beauty of Pakistan with your own eyes. Nothing can compare to standing there in person, taking in the vastness and the majesty of the Karakoram range. Thanks to the expertise of Summit Experts, I felt safe and supported every step of the way. The team’s passion for the mountains and commitment to making sure each trekker has the best possible experience is what really sets them apart. This wasn’t just a trek—it was an unforgettable journey, and I already can’t wait to return. I’m already thinking about next year and planning to do even more trekking in Pakistan. There’s so much more to explore, and I wouldn’t want to do it with anyone else but Summit Experts. If you’re considering an adventure in Pakistan, I cannot recommend this company enough. Thank you, Summit Experts, for an experience I’ll never forget.

 Posted on Tripadvisor  
 
  
 
 
 Chongdee C 
 
 
 
 Verified 
Beyond the ordinary
It took me some time to find the right words to capture the incredible memories we created during our trip to northern Pakistan this April—blossom season at its absolute best! The breathtaking views, the warmth of the people, and the richness of the culture left a lasting impression on me, all made even more special by the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team. Their approach was not just professional but also incredibly humble and flexible, ensuring we had an unforgettable experience. Our group of five Thai friends explored Skardu, Hunza, Passu, and Gilgit at the peak of blossom season. Guided by the company’s CEO, Shah, whose extensive expertise in hiking and expeditions was evident, we found ourselves on a well-planned yet refreshingly adaptable journey. We appreciated how our tour leader went above and beyond, recommending exclusive experiences—from an insightful cultural visit to a local Pakistani home to a glacier trek using a unique route. Unlike standard itineraries, this allowed us to truly get up close and touch the glacier, all while ensuring our safety with expert guidance. One of the highlights was our trek to Fairy Meadows. With hours of hiking ahead, our guide was highly attentive, carefully assessing the natural conditions and our group’s well-being, which made us feel completely safe every step of the way. I already can't wait to return to Pakistan in summer, autumn, and beyond! 😊 A little tip for fellow travelers: If you plan to visit areas that require trekking and hiking, I highly recommend familiarizing yourself with the terrain beforehand. You can always check with the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team about the travel conditions—just to be prepared, not to opt out! The beauty of northern Pakistan is absolutely worth the effort.

I don’t add pictures, because you MUST visit and see all the beauty of Pakistan with your own eyes. The team’s passion for the mountains and commitment to making sure each trekker has the best possible experience is what really sets them apart. Beyond the ordinary
It took me some time to find the right words to capture the incredible memories we created during our trip to northern Pakistan this April—blossom season at its absolute best! The breathtaking views, the warmth of the people, and the richness of the culture left a lasting impression on me, all made even more special by the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team. Their approach was not just professional but also incredibly humble and flexible, ensuring we had an unforgettable experience. Our group of five Thai friends explored Skardu, Hunza, Passu, and Gilgit at the peak of blossom season. Guided by the company’s CEO, Shah, whose extensive expertise in hiking and expeditions was evident, we found ourselves on a well-planned yet refreshingly adaptable journey. We appreciated how our tour leader went above and beyond, recommending exclusive experiences—from an insightful cultural visit to a local Pakistani home to a glacier trek using a unique route. Unlike standard itineraries, this allowed us to truly get up close and touch the glacier, all while ensuring our safety with expert guidance. One of the highlights was our trek to Fairy Meadows. With hours of hiking ahead, our guide was highly attentive, carefully assessing the natural conditions and our group’s well-being, which made us feel completely safe every step of the way. I already can't wait to return to Pakistan in summer, autumn, and beyond! 😊 A little tip for fellow travelers: If you plan to visit areas that require trekking and hiking, I highly recommend familiarizing yourself with the terrain beforehand. You can always check with the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team about the travel conditions—just to be prepared, not to opt out! The beauty of northern Pakistan is absolutely worth the effort.

A Journey to Remember
I just returned from an incredible month-long adventure in northern Pakistan with Summit Experts Adventure Tours. We trekked through some of the most breathtaking regions: Skardu, Hunza, Shimshal Village, and made our way to Shimshal Pass, ending with the exhilarating summit of Manglik Sar (6050m). From the very first moment, I knew I was in the hands of true professionals. The entire trip was perfectly organized, from the logistics to safety measures. But what truly made this experience stand out was the team. Every single person was warm, supportive, and treated me like family. Over the course of the trek, they all became a second family to me, and I genuinely feel like I’ve made lifelong friends. The beauty of the Karakoram combined with the knowledge, passion, and dedication of the Summit Experts team made this adventure unforgettable. I felt supported, safe, and inspired every single day. I don’t add pictures, because you MUST visit and see all the beauty of Pakistan with your own eyes. Nothing can compare to standing there in person, taking in the vastness and the majesty of the Karakoram range. Thanks to the expertise of Summit Experts, I felt safe and supported every step of the way. The team’s passion for the mountains and commitment to making sure each trekker has the best possible experience is what really sets them apart. This wasn’t just a trek—it was an unforgettable journey, and I already can’t wait to return. I’m already thinking about next year and planning to do even more trekking in Pakistan. There’s so much more to explore, and I wouldn’t want to do it with anyone else but Summit Experts. If you’re considering an adventure in Pakistan, I cannot recommend this company enough. Thank you, Summit Experts, for an experience I’ll never forget.

 Posted on Tripadvisor  
 
  
 
 
 Chongdee C 
 
 
 
 Verified 
Beyond the ordinary
It took me some time to find the right words to capture the incredible memories we created during our trip to northern Pakistan this April—blossom season at its absolute best! The breathtaking views, the warmth of the people, and the richness of the culture left a lasting impression on me, all made even more special by the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team. Their approach was not just professional but also incredibly humble and flexible, ensuring we had an unforgettable experience. Our group of five Thai friends explored Skardu, Hunza, Passu, and Gilgit at the peak of blossom season. Guided by the company’s CEO, Shah, whose extensive expertise in hiking and expeditions was evident, we found ourselves on a well-planned yet refreshingly adaptable journey. We appreciated how our tour leader went above and beyond, recommending exclusive experiences—from an insightful cultural visit to a local Pakistani home to a glacier trek using a unique route. Unlike standard itineraries, this allowed us to truly get up close and touch the glacier, all while ensuring our safety with expert guidance. One of the highlights was our trek to Fairy Meadows. With hours of hiking ahead, our guide was highly attentive, carefully assessing the natural conditions and our group’s well-being, which made us feel completely safe every step of the way. I already can't wait to return to Pakistan in summer, autumn, and beyond! 😊 A little tip for fellow travelers: If you plan to visit areas that require trekking and hiking, I highly recommend familiarizing yourself with the terrain beforehand. You can always check with the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team about the travel conditions—just to be prepared, not to opt out! The beauty of northern Pakistan is absolutely worth the effort.

But what truly made this experience stand out was the team. Every single person was warm, supportive, and treated me like family. Over the course of the trek, they all became a second family to me, and I genuinely feel like I’ve made lifelong friends. The beauty of the Karakoram combined with the knowledge, passion, and dedication of the Summit Experts team made this adventure unforgettable. I felt supported, safe, and inspired every single day. I don’t add pictures, because you MUST visit and see all the beauty of Pakistan with your own eyes. Nothing can compare to standing there in person, taking in the vastness and the majesty of the Karakoram range. Thanks to the expertise of Summit Experts, I felt safe and supported every step of the way. The team’s passion for the mountains and commitment to making sure each trekker has the best possible experience is what really sets them apart. This wasn’t just a trek—it was an unforgettable journey, and I already can’t wait to return. I’m already thinking about next year and planning to do even more trekking in Pakistan. There’s so much more to explore, and I wouldn’t want to do it with anyone else but Summit Experts. If you’re considering an adventure in Pakistan, I cannot recommend this company enough. Why Pakistan

Why Explore Pakistan?

From the highest peaks on Earth to ancient Silk Road valleys, Pakistan offers an unmatched blend of adventure, history, and natural beauty — still raw, still uncrowded, still waiting to be discovered.

Explore Adventures
Discover Tours

What Makes
Pakistan Special?

Pakistan is a land of extraordinary diversity, where towering mountains, ancient cultures, and warm hospitality meet in a single journey. In the north, the Karakoram, Himalaya, and Hindukush ranges rise together — nowhere else on the planet do three of the world’s great mountain systems converge so closely. Here you can trek beneath K2, cross glaciers older than memory, and wake to sunrise over valleys few outsiders have ever seen.

But Pakistan is far more than its summits. It is the orchards and stone forts of Hunza, the Buddhist heritage of the ancient Silk Road, vibrant mountain festivals, and the legendary hospitality of its people — where a stranger is welcomed as a guest and a guest as family. Every journey here is a blend of thrilling adventure and genuine cultural immersion.

And perhaps best of all: Pakistan remains one of the last great travel frontiers. While the world’s famous trails grow crowded, our mountains and valleys stay wild, authentic, and unspoiled.

Explore Adventure

Home to Three of the World's Greatest Mountain Ranges

In the north of Pakistan, the Karakoram, Himalaya, and Hindukush ranges come together in one breathtaking region — a meeting of giants found nowhere else on Earth. This is the land of K2, Nanga Parbat, and the Baltoro Glacier; of high passes, alpine meadows, and some of the most dramatic scenery on the planet.

A Living Culture, Thousands of Years Deep

Beyond the mountains lies a cultural landscape just as rich. Pakistan is home to ancient civilizations, centuries-old forts, and traditions still alive in the valleys today.

Wander the 700-year-old Baltit and Altit Forts of Hunza. Follow the legendary Karakoram Highway, tracing one of the original routes of the ancient Silk Road. Witness the colour of mountain festivals — the Shandur Polo Festival, played on the highest polo ground in the world, and the living traditions of the valleys of Gilgit-Baltistan and Chitral. Taste the food, hear the music, and experience the warmth that has made Pakistani hospitality famous across the world.

For travellers who want more than a view, Pakistan offers a story — one you don’t just see, but feel.

Why Choose Pakistan for Your Next Trip?

Pakistan offers a one-of-a-kind experience that combines world-class adventure with authentic cultural immersion — and exceptional value. Whether you are scaling an 8,000-metre peak, exploring ancient landmarks, or simply soaking in landscapes that seem to stretch forever, Pakistan is a destination that truly has it all.

It is also remarkably accessible: online tourist visas are now available to travellers from most of the world, the northern tourist regions are welcoming and well-travelled, and your budget stretches far further here than in Europe, North America, or much of Asia.

108+ Peaks Above 7,000 Meters
